metas.name: Sweden - Blekinge
metas.note: Blekinge uses these two pictured bus stop designs. Their bus company, BlekingeTrafiken, will show up on their buses.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Dalarna
metas.note: Dalarna bus stop signs (and buses too actually) will have the county logo which is a stylistic horse with diagonal lines coming out of the bottom and left sides.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Gavleborg
metas.note: The Gavleborg bus company is called Xtrafik and this will show up on their bus stop signs. In addition, their buses will have a large X in the style of the logo.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Gotland
metas.note: Gotland bus stop signs are yellow with green stripes as depicted. The bus company logo, which is a triangle of 3 leaves, will show up on the sides of buses occasionally (might be colored differently).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Halland
metas.note: The most distinct part of Halland buses is the "H" logo, as its left side features a rough profile of the coastline of Halland county.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Jamtland
metas.note: In Jamtland, the buses and bus stops feature the bus company logo, which is a Z enclosed in a diamond shape. It should be visible from decently far away even in the blurriest gen 2 coverage.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Jonkoping
metas.note: Jonkoping county is run by the Lanstrafiken bus company, with its logo being a distinct profile of a reclining bus seat.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Kalmar
metas.note: Kalmar has this heart shaped bus logo as well as these yellow and red buses.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Kronoberg
metas.note: Green, green, everywhere. The bus signs are green, the buses are green, and the logo is a technology bank company looking green swoosh.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Norrbotten
metas.note: Norrbotten has this as their current bus stop sign. They also have these very distinct and common bus stop shelters, which are very high-yield to learn as it immediately gives away the region from a distance.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Orebro
metas.note: Orebro has blue signs with the LT logo clearly visible.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Ostergotland
metas.note: Ostergotland has this style of bus sign (general color scheme is the same but the layout may change ever-so slightly). The logo will appear too, which is a red stylized french horn shape, albeit a bit small.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Skane

metas.name: Sweden - Sormland
metas.note: Sodermanland uses these lime green bus stop signs, and the bus company logo is two outward facing arrows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Stockholm
metas.note: Stockholm bus stop signs are usually red, but should always have the SL logo with the half-circle rings below the letters.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Uppsala
metas.note: Uppsala uses black and yellow bus stop signs and have a UL logo for the company. They also have these red bus shelters with the red shingle roofs, which can also be found in the neighboring Varmland county albeit with slightly less steep roof angle.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Varmland
metas.note: The green and yellow shark fin shaped logo is the most distinct feature of both the bus stops and the buses in Varmland
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Vasterbotten
metas.note: In Vasterbotten, you will find these blue and white bus stop signs, with the company logo being a group of three blue arrows vaguely resembling a stylized evergreen tree. In addition, this region has distinct and unique blue wooden bus stop shelters that are quite useful to determine the region from a distance.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Vasternorrland
metas.note: Vasternorrland bus infrastructure is obsessed with this "Din Tur" text and the green and yellow logo, with it appearing on most relevant bus infrastructure in the county.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Vastmanland
metas.note: Vastmanland has a VL bus company with this relatively basic logo and a similarly basic bus stop sign with just the logo and a white background. Even though it's quite generic, the logo still sticks out once you know to look for it.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Vastra Gotaland
metas.note: Vastra Gotaland has this health organization looking checkmark logo, which shows up on their bus stop signs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.
